::::: {.home-start}
::::::: {.home-start-intro}
## Quick start

Install Panache, then format and lint your first document.

Prefer a package manager? See the [installation
guide](getting-started.qmd#installation) for Homebrew, npm, uv, Cargo, and other
options.

Using VS Code or Positron? The [Panache
extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=jolars.panache)
installs the CLI and starts the language server for you. See [editor
setup](guide/lsp.qmd) for other editors.
:::::::

::::::: {.home-start-commands}
::::::::: {.panel-tabset}
### macOS and Linux

```sh
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://panache.bz/install | sh
```

### Windows

```powershell
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command "irm https://panache.bz/install.ps1 | iex"
```
:::::::::

Then put Panache to work:

```sh
panache format document.qmd
panache lint document.qmd
```
:::::::
:::::

::::: {#where-to-go-next .home-details}
::::::: {.home-detail}
## Your Markdown, understood

Quarto, Pandoc, R Markdown, MyST, CommonMark, and GitHub Flavored Markdown each
have their own syntax. Panache parses your document with its flavor in mind,
from a simple README to a paper with citations, grid tables, and inline
footnotes.

[Explore the user guide](guide/index.qmd) or see how Panache [compares with
other tools](guide/comparison.qmd).
:::::::

::::::: {.home-detail}
## Bring your code tools along

Use your preferred formatters and linters inside code blocks, including Ruff for
Python and Air for R. Panache handles the surrounding document and maps code
diagnostics back to their source.

[Configure embedded code
tools](guide/configure.qmd#configure-linting-and-embedded-code) and [tune
Panache for your project](guide/configure.qmd).
:::::::
:::::
:::
